abstract1.1.text: We study the problem of sampling from μ ⁡ ( d ​ x ) ∝ e − V ⁡ ( x ) ​ d ​ x \mu(\mathrm{d}x)\propto e^{-V(x)}\,\mathrm{d}x on ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} , where V V is α \alpha -strongly convex and β \beta -smooth, and write κ ≔ β / α \kappa\coloneqq\beta/\alpha . We design and analyze the Proximal Bouncy Particle Sampler (Proximal BPS), a new sampler that combines ideas from the proximal sampler and the bouncy particle sampler. From a warm start initialization with O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) Rényi divergence w.r.t. μ \mu , Proximal BPS returns a sample whose law is ε \varepsilon -close to μ \mu in total variation distance using O ~ ​ ( κ ​ d 1 / 4 ​ polylog ​ ( 1 / ε ) ) \widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\kappa}\,d^{1/4}\,\mathrm{polylog}(1/\varepsilon)) gradient queries in expectation.

S2.SS1.p1.5.text: The bounce update is p ← R ∇ V ​ ( x ) ​ p p\leftarrow R_{\nabla V(x)}p . It preserves ‖ p ‖ \|p\| , leaves the component tangent to a level set unchanged, and reverses the normal component, since ( R h ​ p ) ⊤ ​ h = − p ⊤ ​ h (R_{h}p)^{\top}h=-p^{\top}h . Thus, the particle travels freely while moving down the potential and bounces, at a rate equal to its instantaneous uphill directional derivative, when it moves up the potential. Proximal BPS reuses this bounce mechanism, applied to a localized conditional target; the construction is given in Section 3 .
